q1.prompt: You need all keys sharing a prefix of length L. Which structure pays O(L), not O(number of keys)?

choices.label: Trie — walk one edge per character from the root
Hash set — scan every key and compare prefixes

wrong_hash.prompt: A hash set only helps exact lookup.
wrong_hash.explanation: Prefix search on a hash set scans keys. A trie shares paths so insert and prefix walk cost O(L) for string length L.

q2.prompt: Which workload is too simple to justify a trie?

choices.label: When you only need exact lookup — a hash set is simpler
Never — tries beat hashes for every string store

wrong_refuse.prompt: Exact lookup does not need a trie.
wrong_refuse.explanation: Avoid a trie when you only need exact lookup — a hash set is simpler. Avoid a 26-slot array design for huge Unicode alphabets without compression. Avoid building a trie when n and L make memory the bottleneck.

success.prompt: You matched tries to prefix walks and avoided them for plain exact lookup.
